# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Instructions for Element Inspector This document provides instructions for AI coding agents (Claude Code, etc.) on how to interpret and act on element inspector data from this Next.js photography site. ## Element Inspector Overview The development-mode element inspector allows the site owner to hover over UI elements and generate AI-ready prompts. When you receive a prompt from the inspector, it will follow one of these formats: ### Standard Element Prompt ``` Element ID: header-1 Component: Header at components/Header.jsx Current classes: 'bg-black text-white py-6' Instruction: [User's instruction] ``` ### Cloudinary Image Prompt ``` Element ID: cloudinaryimage-5 Component: CloudinaryImage at components/CloudinaryImage.jsx Cloudinary Settings: Source: https://res.cloudinary.com/.../photo.jpg Quality: auto Format: auto Width: 800 Instruction: [User's instruction] ``` ## How to Interpret Element IDs Element IDs follow the pattern `{componentname}-{number}`: - `header-1` → The Header component (`components/Header.jsx`) - `footer-2` → The Footer component (`components/Footer.jsx`) - `cloudinaryimage-3` → A CloudinaryImage instance (`components/CloudinaryImage.jsx`) - `photoslider-4` → The PhotoSlider carousel (`components/PhotoSlider.jsx`) - `categorygrid-5` → The CategoryGrid gallery (`components/CategoryGrid.jsx`) - `roompreviews-6` → The RoomPreviews component (`components/RoomPreviews.jsx`) ## Component File Locations | Component | File | Purpose | |-----------|------|---------| | Header | `components/Header.jsx` | Site navigation and title bar | | Footer | `components/Footer.jsx` | Social links, bio, contact | | CloudinaryImage | `components/CloudinaryImage.jsx` | Optimized image display with Cloudinary | | PhotoSlider | `components/PhotoSlider.jsx` | Hero image carousel on homepage | | CategoryGrid | `components/CategoryGrid.jsx` | Gallery category grid | | RoomPreviews | `components/RoomPreviews.jsx` | Room preview with photo overlay | ## Styling Guidelines This project uses **Tailwind CSS 4.x**. When modifying styles: ### Common Layout Changes - **Centering**: Use `mx-auto`, `text-center`, `flex justify-center items-center` - **Spacing**: Use `p-{n}`, `m-{n}`, `gap-{n}`, `space-y-{n}`, `space-x-{n}` - **Sizing**: Use `w-{value}`, `h-{value}`, `max-w-{value}` - **Responsive**: Prefix with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:` for breakpoints ### Example Modifications **"Make the header title larger"**: ```jsx // In components/Header.jsx, change:

// To:

``` **"Center this paragraph more"**: ```jsx // Add text-center and mx-auto classes

``` **"Add more space between items"**: ```jsx // Increase gap value

→
``` ## Cloudinary Image Adjustments Images use Cloudinary CDN with URL-based transformations. The loader is at `lib/cloudinaryLoader.js`. ### Current Transformation Format ``` https://res.cloudinary.com/{cloud}/image/upload/f_auto,q_{quality},w_{width}/{image_path} ``` ### Adjusting Image Quality (Reducing "Fuzziness") To make an image sharper/clearer: 1. Set explicit quality (higher = clearer, larger file): `q_80`, `q_90`, `q_100` 2. Add sharpening: `e_sharpen:100` (0-100 scale) 3. Increase delivered width: `w_1200` instead of `w_800` To modify how CloudinaryImage handles quality, edit `lib/cloudinaryLoader.js`: ```javascript // Current: uses auto quality `f_auto,q_${quality || 'auto'},w_${width}` // For explicit quality control, pass quality prop to CloudinaryImage component ``` ### Example: Making a Photo Clearer ```jsx // The CloudinaryImage component at components/CloudinaryImage.jsx // To increase quality for a specific image, modify the cloudinaryLoader.js // or pass quality via the component's src URL transformation ``` ## Important Notes 1. **Development Only**: The inspector only works in `NODE_ENV=development`. gh pr comment 43 --body "$(cat <<'ENDCOMMENT'
## Review Feedback Response

### Critical / Major — Accepted & Fixed

| # | Source | Issue | Action |
|---|--------|-------|--------|
| 1 | GitHub Actions (opencode) | **Missing JSON.parse error handling** in 3 settings GET routes | **Fixed** — added try-catch around `JSON.parse` in settings/images, settings/layout, and photos/image-settings routes. Returns sensible defaults (empty object or DEFAULT_LAYOUT) on parse failure instead of 500. |
| 2 | GitHub Actions (opencode) | **Missing `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`** on all admin routes | **Fixed** — added to all 5 route files. Without this, Next.js could cache GET responses and serve stale admin data. |
| 3 | Macroscope | **Layout settings stored without schema validation** | **Fixed** (prior commit) — validates `gridColumns` (1-12), `colorScheme` (light/dark), and object type. |
| 4 | CodeRabbit | **Port mismatch**: next.config.mjs uses 4010 but docs say 4000 | **Fixed** (prior commit) — updated CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .env.example to 4010. |

### Major — Rejected with Reasoning

| # | Source | Issue | Decision |
|---|--------|-------|----------|
| 5 | CodeRabbit | **Relative URLs conflict with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` guideline** | **Rejected.** This is a false positive. The entire purpose of issue #42 is to move admin endpoints from the backend to local Next.js API routes backed by SQLite. Using `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` for local routes would incorrectly proxy them to the backend. Relative URLs are the correct architecture — the `fallback` rewrite pattern in `next.config.mjs` ensures local routes (auth, admin) take precedence while unmatched requests proxy to the backend. CLAUDE.md has been updated to document this distinction. |

### Minor — Accepted & Fixed

| # | Source | Issue | Action |
|---|--------|-------|--------|
| 6 | CodeRabbit | **`global.Response` mock not restored in test teardown** | **Fixed** — all 5 admin route test files now save `originalResponse` and restore in `afterAll()`. |
| 7 | GitHub Actions | **Inconsistent input validation** across PUT routes | **Fixed** — added object-type validation to images and photo-settings PUT routes for consistency with page and layout routes. |

### Minor — Deferred / Rejected

| # | Source | Issue | Decision |
|---|--------|-------|----------|
| 8 | GitHub Actions | **Duplicate auth code** — extract to helper | **Deferred.** 5 small route files with identical 3-line auth checks don't warrant a shared abstraction yet. Extracting now adds indirection without meaningful DRY benefit. Will revisit if more admin routes are added. |
| 9 | GitHub Actions | **Missing DELETE operations** for pages | **Out of scope.** Issue #42 specifies GET/PUT for pages. DELETE can be added in a follow-up issue if needed. |
| 10 | GitHub Actions | **Payload size limits** | **Not needed.** Next.js enforces a default 4MB body size limit on API routes. Explicit validation adds no value here. |
| 11 | GitHub Actions | **No database indexes** | **Premature.** Admin settings tables have single-digit rows. Indexes would add overhead for zero benefit at this scale. |
| 12 | GitHub Actions | **`jest.resetModules()` is heavy-handed** in admin-db tests | **Intentional.** The tests need a fresh `:memory:` SQLite database per test. `jest.resetModules()` forces a clean module re-import, which is the correct approach for testing module-level lazy initialization. |
ENDCOMMENT
)" 2>&1

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The three hardening patterns applied here are worth noting as a reusable checklist for Next.js API routes:
1. **`export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`** — prevents Next.js from statically caching GET route responses at build time, which is critical for any route reading from a database
2. **JSON.parse try-catch on DB reads** — defensive against corrupted data; returns a safe fallback (`{}`) rather than crashing the route
3. **`afterAll` teardown for global mocks** — Jest test suites that override `global.Response` (or any global) must restore the original to prevent pollution across test files in the same worker
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Summary of what was pushed (commit `3cd55e4`):**

| Change | Files |
|--------|-------|
| `force-dynamic` export | All 5 route handlers |
| JSON.parse error handling | 3 settings GET routes |
| PUT body validation | images + photo-settings routes |
